column3: Issue, Design spec, Pull request, Implementation plan, Post pass, Debrief
column4: Every change moves through spec, plan, draft pull request, kept history and debrief on the tracker, and the three files carry or name those steps.
The commit message carries only what outlives review in a fixed subject form, and prek.toml holds the hooks for the decidable rows.

Each tool runs at its strictest setting with exclusions named beside the code, configuration exists only where it deviates, and lint levels live only in Cargo.toml, so every tool configuration, every place a lint flag could be passed and every inline exclusion is bound.
Every tracked file must reach an actor through .readers, so adding a file at any path can break it; ** is honest for additions although only .readers is bound for content.
The flat actor roster lives in this record and the readers check takes each name from its CONTEXT.md anchor, so the roster, the anchors, the bindings and the check are bound.
Every artifact holds only what conveys its point and provenance crosses every location, so the sufficiency rule binds everything written; the decidable rules are a subset over records.

column3: Issue, Design spec, Pull request, Debrief
column4: Issue bodies, titles and specs are rewritten until the type is set, pull request bodies until merge, supersession follows a fixed procedure, and AGENTS.md and the sign.yml thread carry the agreement.
A question no title answers gets a new record and every title states each decision its record holds; binds the records, the template and AGENTS.md, which carries the rule.
Shell and Rust changes are built test-first, with the test list in the plan and a failing test-only push on the pull request; prose and configuration owe no test.
Two-space indentation is stated once for every language that admits it, in the one style location .editorconfig.
A fork pull request never merges and a maintainer applies it with the script to accepted/pr-<n>, keeping author and trailers; sign.yml and the ruleset hold the refusal.
A code comment is written only when no other location holds the information and cites a source rather than an issue; the comment is pathless and the link gate's files hold the decidable part.
Records are proposition-titled files with four ordered sections, no issue numbers and proposition citations, replaced rather than amended; binds the records and the command that checks them.

column3: Published comment, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:wiki, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:discussions, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:public docs site
column4: Each register is written where its location's author reads it and defines no word, and no location opens without a reader and a register; binds the register files, which artifact earns a published comment, and the closed locations.
No gate may stand over a judgement, so every place a refusal can be wired is bound: workflows, gate scripts, tasks and the ruleset.
A term is defined once in CONTEXT.md as a heading with one or two sentences and no outbound link, and a record names it without holding it.
An act GITHUB_TOKEN cannot perform gets a scoped App identity and Actions' token is never widened; binds the workflows, the failure reporter's token, the setting and the App's permissions.

Origin, authorship and acceptance are trailers written from the act of the party that makes each true, and stewardship lives in CODEOWNERS; binds the commit message, the sign job and its scripts, and the settings it reads.
mise.toml and its committed lock name every tool, lockfiles are marked generated, README states the host C toolchain and each workflow names mise; a second manager's file would break it.
Each package is declared in exactly one of three manifests by a stated rule, and lint:manifests compares them.
Each pull request answers one issue and says so when a second rides along; no file is bound.
A script lives in the half of the tree its callers live in and CODEOWNERS covers both halves; binds both script directories and every file the record names as a caller.
Record prose obeys the borrowed sentence, paragraph, -ing and tense rules that check-records.sh refuses or reports.
mise is the only tool manager, its manifest and lock are committed with lockfiles marked generated, README states the host C toolchain, and build.yml proves the extension loads.
purba stays on nightly for the new solver, the product crate takes no nightly-only feature without a stable fallback, and a use outside it names its fallback on its issue.
Four ruff crates are pinned exactly, named at the first call site, behind one parsing module.
Mostly a ruling that nothing claims to separate a person from their agent; the sign-off helper, which must claim no more than it checks, is the one file it binds.
The Python floor is computed by the two-year rule and carried in the five locations the record names.
Scripts are bash with bats tests ending in .bats, workflow shell stays shell except the Python in build.yml, and the bats roster entry, task and globs carry it.
A change is significant if and only if it adds or changes a record, and CODEOWNERS with the ruleset routes it to the code owner.
The agent that marks a pull request ready acts on each review before anyone asks, and AGENTS.md carries the rule.
Cargo.toml declares cdylib and rlib, extension-module as a named feature and the rustdoc lint, and doc tests over Rust fences run through tasks.toml and quality.yml.
The nightly is a date named once in mise.toml and recorded in mise.lock, no rust-toolchain.toml exists, and bump.yml proposes the next date.
The person owns each record's Decision Outcome, routed by CODEOWNERS and the required code-owner review.
